workflow_rationale: Single service, single file modification. Adding a security header to next.config.ts is a straightforward task with no multi-service dependencies or staged migration requirements. Classified as 'simple' to minimize planning overhead.

phases.name: Add CSP Header
phases.description: Add Content Security Policy header to next.config.ts to provide defense-in-depth against XSS attacks

implementation_notes: Add CSP header to existing headers array in async headers() function
CSP must allow: inline styles (Tailwind), same-origin scripts, Supabase API, data: URIs for images
CSP must block: unsafe-eval, external script sources
Preserve existing security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy)

verification.instructions: Start dev server, check browser Network tab for CSP header presence and correct value

subtasks.notes:
Successfully added Content-Security-Policy header to next.config.ts. The CSP header includes:
- default-src 'self' - Only allow resources from same origin by default
- script-src 'self' - Only allow scripts from same origin
- style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' - Allow same-origin and inline styles (required for Tailwind CSS)
- img-src 'self' data: https: - Allow images from same origin, data URIs (for QR codes), and HTTPS URLs
- connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co - Allow API connections to same origin and Supabase
- font-src 'self' - Only allow fonts from same origin
- object-src 'none' - Block all object/embed/applet elements
- base-uri 'self' - Restrict base tag to same origin
- form-action 'self' - Only allow form submissions to same origin
- frame-ancestors 'none' - Prevent framing (redundant with X-Frame-Options but part of CSP)

This provides defense-in-depth protection against XSS attacks while supporting the application's requirements. Manual verification required: start dev server and check browser Network tab for CSP header.
